chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him, 'When we enter Mecca and Medina, do we complete the prayer or shorten it?' He said, 'If you shorten it, that is acceptable; and if you complete it, that is better, you will increase [in reward].'
ai.seo_question: Should Muslims shorten or complete their prayers when visiting Mecca and Medina?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the permissibility of shortening prayers in the two holy sanctuaries is affirmed, yet completing them is highlighted as the superior act of worship. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic view that while the concession of qasr remains valid in Mecca and Medina, the spiritual merit of tamm is preferred due to the heightened sanctity of these locations. The chain of transmission through Abu Ibrahim (Imam al-Sadiq) underscores the direct prophetic authority behind this practical guidance for pilgrims.
